messages:
Maria Lopez: quick Q — behavior question for API auth: if client sends a valid org-scoped API key but omits X-Project-ID header, should we return 400, 401, or 403? trying to be strict but avoid breaking older clients.
Alex Chen: my read: missing required header -> 400 bad request. auth is orthogonal.
Jen Ortiz: hmm we currently treat project-scoped keys as requiring X-Project-ID for routing. if none, we fallback to org default project in some services. that's the inconsistency.
Samir Patel: agree with Alex for public APIs, but for internal endpoints we do 401 when key lacks scope. Need clarity: is this endpoint expecting project scoping or optional?
Maria Lopez: endpoint is /v1/usage/claims — it's intended to be project-scoped, but a bunch of older SDKs didn't send X-Project-ID. we have a migration window.
Alex Chen: ok if we want graceful: prefer 200 with tenancy inferred? risky. alternative: return 403 with body explaining missing header and link to migration doc.
Jen Ortiz: can we return 401? semantically 401 = invalid/unauth. If key is valid but header missing, 403 sounds more accurate but clients will be confused.
Samir Patel: what about 428 Precondition Required? not widely used but accurate.
Maria Lopez: leaning towards 400 + structured error code so SDKs can auto-detect. e.g. {"error":"missing_header","header":"X-Project-ID","code":"missing_project_id"} and 30d grace in logs.
Alex Chen: +1 for 400 with machine-friendly error. keeps auth semantics separate.
Jen Ortiz: works for me. caveat: routing layer needs to stop falling back to org default for this endpoint asap. I'll open a PR to remove fallback.
Samir Patel: I'll add a gate in the runtime to emit a deprecation metric when X-Project-ID is absent but key is org-scoped. helps us track rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: remove-org-fallback-in-routing (sha: c8f3a2b) — scheduled for canary 12:00 UTC tomorrow.
Maria Lopez: action items: 1) Jen removes fallback (PR) 2) Sam adds deprec metric + dashboards 3) Alex adds error schema to API spec and updates SDK error handling 4) I'll draft a short migration note for customers and add to changelog.
Alex Chen: example error payload i'm proposing: ```json
{
  "error": {
    "type": "missing_header",
    "message": "X-Project-ID header required for project-scoped keys",
    "code": "missing_project_id",
    "help_url": "https://redwood.example.com/docs/migration/x-project-id"
  }
}
```
Jen Ortiz: can we also include a hint field with expected project id when key maps cleanly to a single project? maybe only in internal logs, not response.
Samir Patel: yeah logs only. do not leak project IDs in client-facing errors. security concern.
Maria Lopez: agreed — no project IDs in responses. logs → alerting for obvious high-volume offenders.
Alex Chen: final note: backward compat plan: return 400 for now, start canary after routing fallback is removed, then after 30 days flip to 403 for stricter enforcement if needed.
Maria Lopez: perfect. thanks all. ping me in thread when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
